replies.text:
You’re describing a Ponzi Scheme, and you are essentially correct!  With dwindling birth rates GDP and output gets reduced.  Inflation has to occur to support debt and interest rates.  Inflation is cause both by money printing/supply, and via supply/demand factors.  As long as enough people have money or credit to buy/spend businesses will continue to increase prices until demand is meaningfully reduced.  That recession then triggers lower prices, and stagnates them for a while til people are comfortable enough to spend again.  So long as your peers are willing to pay $6-8 for a loaf of bread, $12-15/lb for tri tip steak etc the stores will keep charging that and higher til the demand is reduced and the prices find equilibrium.  So your budget and related inflation is always in relation to your peers.  That’s why Investing and Asset Ownership is important.  

If your peers live below their means (delay gratification, spend less), or work harder than you (produce or make more), and invest in the Stock Market, Assets (homes or other assets), and/or investment in starting a business etc, over time they develop disposable income and assets that allow them to spend when you are tight. A dollar saved is a dollar earned philosophy.  Having Investments and Assets that out pace inflation (you have cash when others don’t, so you can buy when they can’t) means you are beating inflation.  Inflation impoverishes those without investments and Assets and benefits those with Good Debt and assets.  Good debt being fixed rates that the interest expense is eroded away by inflation while the underlying Asset Value goes up also via inflation (think fixed mortgage on real estate; particularly investment properties).  

Over time, Asset Values Increase.  Those with Investment Assets benefit from inflation from the value increasing and the debt service interest expense being eroded by inflation.  Think of a 30 year mortgage.  In year 1 the payment may feel tight for your given budget/income, but the future brings pay raises comparable to inflation (generally speaking over long term), 10, 15, 20 years later your mortgage payment (principal and interest total) has not changed at all yet it’s easier for you to afford it with extra cash each month for other spending.  Year one you maybe took home $5K and paid $2K on the mortgage, in year 15 you take home $8K but still have a $2K mortgage.  Inflation erodes the interest expense’s effect on your budget and you have an extra $3K to additionally invest or otherwise spend.  

Historical Stock Market long term averages about 10.5%/Yr, compared to inflation at about 3%.  RE values exceed 3% growth and are also benefiting from the mortgage pay down some each month (principal reduction).  

So, both of those investment mechanisms outpace inflation, generally.  Those without Assets live paycheck to paycheck in perpetuity hoping their pay raises offset inflation.

replies.text:
I'm not sure I understand what you mean. In what sense is the house a converted asset? The house still exists, is tangible, and can be traded as such. Do you mean the original owner has converted the house into cash? Because that's nothing to do with the nature of the house that's just describing a trade. You are perhaps confusing "value" with "money".

The point of the example, and this is remarkable, is that a loan from a bank is not like a loan from your uncle. When you uncle loans you money to buy a house, he has to actually have that money and trade it to you for an IOU. When a bank loans you money to buy a house, they don't need to have the money. They can just create deposits from whole cloth, and simultaneously recieve the IOU. Crucially, it is these bank deposits which are accepted as money. Saying "banks create money" looses some of this subtlety. They can't create cash, but they can create deposits which can be traded for cash. Both bank deposits and cash fall under the umbrella of "money". Licensed banks can do this (within limits set by capital and liquidity rules); your uncle can't. 

In the case of a mortgage, that money they create immediately gets paid to the person selling the house. The fact that the mortgage is a loan for a specific purchase adds a layer of obfuscation - it is irrelevant for the point the video is making, which is just about loans in general. In fact, with a mortgage, the money from the sale is often used to pay off the rest of the seller's own mortgage, *destroying* money.
